hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2521.meaning: Life’s rhythms change; we must adapt our actions to the varying conditions around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2521.context: Vedic actions have qualities, seasons are not always pleasant, and so are the times.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2650.meaning: Even the planet creates safety for the lowest beings, showing nature’s care.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2650.context: The earth itself made a special protective zone for the lowest world.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2651.meaning: Different roles use different tools to protect and serve society.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2651.context: Brahmins gain power through study and prayer, while warriors gain strength through weapons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2652.meaning: Unity and care are important, yet we may face judgment for our actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2652.context: People should stay together and help each other, but the speaker feels criticized.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2653.meaning: We should seek help from nature, trusting it will provide what we need.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2653.context: The speaker asks the earth to give all its resources, even though rules are unclear.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2655.meaning: True wisdom keeps calm and follows right action, even when surprised.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2655.context: King Vaishravana is surprised, but the wise man remains calm and follows duty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2657.meaning: Respecting higher truth leads to victory and lasting honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2657.context: A king who knows the divine respects it, conquers evil, and gains fame.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2659.meaning: Every person’s daily actions shape the world’s balance and purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2659.context: A Brahmin drinks water, an old man, and a warrior use weapons daily.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2660.meaning: Good deeds uplift people and bring peace to our own lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2660.context: The king’s work improves humanity and conquers the body of his father.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2663.meaning: When leaders follow the right path, everyone respects them. Good leadership brings peace and order to society.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2663.context: The text explains that kings follow sacred law, so people respect them everywhere in the land.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2664.meaning: Justice is strict and fair. It does not forgive those who harm others or act with selfish greed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2664.context: This verse describes a powerful force that punishes wrongdoers and thieves without showing any mercy at all.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2665.meaning: Leaders must protect what is right. When they do, the whole community stays safe and morally upright.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2665.context: The king protects the moral laws that people follow, ensuring that righteousness stays strong in the nation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2666.meaning: A good leader studies, gives, and worships. They rule with care and fairness for everyone under them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2666.context: King Bhaka is praised for his good deeds, worship, and fair rule over his people in ancient times.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2667.meaning: Leaders and people need each other. When problems arise, the community stands together to support the ruler.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2667.context: The people support their king when things go wrong, showing that the ruler and citizens depend on each other.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2668.meaning: Cruel and dishonest leaders are the worst. They bring harm to society and should be avoided at all costs.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2668.context: The text warns against cruel rulers who lie and act badly, describing them as the lowest type of leader.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2669.meaning: Prevention is better than cure. It is much harder to fix a loss than to stop it from happening.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2669.context: The verse states that stolen money is very hard to get back once thieves have taken it away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2670.meaning: We must respect and protect those who guide us spiritually. Hurting them is a serious wrong that brings bad karma.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_2670.context: The text says all people must protect the priests and holy men, as they are very important to society.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4030.meaning: You do not need to be scared of dying because your soul is eternal and always safe.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4030.context: A wise teacher tells a student that they are safe and free from all danger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4032.meaning: When you live with joy and peace, your spirit shines brightly and feels free from fear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4032.context: A bright, golden body moves into a forest where a character named Chitranga lives happily.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4033.meaning: Fear makes you run away, but true strength comes from facing your fears calmly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4033.context: A frightened person runs away while a young tiger looks hungry and ready to attack.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4034.meaning: Spending time with wise people helps you grow strong and earn the respect of others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4034.context: A person stays with a sage and becomes strong like a tiger, earning respect from others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4035.meaning: When you reach a higher level of power, you no longer need basic things to feel full.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4035.context: A strong animal body becomes a tiger and stops wanting simple food like roots and fruits.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4046.meaning: You should spend time with people who are like you to feel safe and understood.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4046.context: A sage guides a snake lord to a lion and tells him to stay with his own kind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4047.meaning: Even if you win a fight, you may still feel sad if you are alone in the wild.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4047.context: A strong voice kills a lion, but the person living in the forest is not happy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4048.meaning: Small creatures feel scared all the time because they are always worried about staying alive.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_4048.context: Small animals live in a holy forest, feeling scared and always trying to stay alive.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5047.meaning: When leaders step down, communities lose direction, and celebrations can fade if not supported by people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5047.context: Agriculture grew, cows were protected, and trade stopped. A festival ended when a leader retired.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5049.meaning: A once lively place can become silent and haunted when people leave or are destroyed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5049.context: Bones and skeletons crowded, ghosts linger. An empty city looks like a burnt village.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5050.meaning: Violence and mistrust make people withdraw, leaving places lonely and unsafe.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5050.context: Thieves, weapons, and kings caused fear. The land felt empty and desolate.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5051.meaning: When wisdom and care disappear, nature and society become broken and lifeless.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5051.context: Brahmins were killed, protection lost, herbs vanished. Earth looked like a ghostly man lying down.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5053.meaning: Without moral strength, people turn on each other, harming themselves and their community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5053.context: Fear of enemies, righteousness exhausted. Yudhisthira saw hungry people eating each other.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5063.meaning: Even in despair, one can seek purpose and hope, refusing to let death feel pointless.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5063.context: The sage wondered what good he could do. He questioned death’s meaning.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5064.meaning: Seeing death’s harsh reality reminds us that violence destroys both body and dignity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5064.context: The sage saw dead flesh spread. A king in a lowly house was killed by a weapon.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5065.meaning: Choosing the right action is the only way to protect people and maintain peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5065.context: He thought he should act right. No other way to keep others safe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5665.meaning: Understanding Vivitsa's teachings can be confusing. It's important to seek truth and wisdom from reliable sources for guidance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5665.context: In Hinduism, the Mahabharata tells a story about the conflict between the Pandavas and Kauravas. This verse discusses the contrasting teachings of Vivitsa, who promotes conflicting scriptures.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5666.meaning: Attachment to wealth leads to madness. Seeking wisdom and knowledge can help one overcome this attachment and attain sanity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5666.context: The verse talks about the consequences of attachment to wealth and how knowledge can overcome it.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5668.meaning: Jealousy hinders compassion. Cultivating righteousness leads to the growth of compassion and inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5668.context: The verse discusses jealousy and its impact on compassion, as well as the importance of righteousness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5669.meaning: Negative influences can confuse us. By focusing on the suffering around us, compassion can be awakened and sustained.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5669.context: The verse highlights the consequences of being influenced by negative words and the power of seeing suffering.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5670.meaning: Vivitsa's teachings can be confusing. Following righteousness leads to inner peace and harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5670.context: The verse talks about the contrasting teachings of Vivitsa and the importance of righteousness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5671.meaning: Attachment to material possessions causes suffering. Detachment leads to inner peace and liberation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5671.context: The verse discusses the consequences of attachment to material possessions and the power of detachment.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5672.meaning: Seeking truth from reliable sources brings clarity and inner peace. Ignoring truth can lead to confusion and suffering.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5672.context: The verse highlights the importance of seeking truth and wisdom from reliable sources.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5673.meaning: Seeing suffering can awaken compassion. Following righteousness brings inner peace and harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_5673.context: The verse emphasizes the power of seeing suffering and the importance of righteousness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6042.meaning: The story shows how power can be used to punish wrongdoers, but it also warns of unfair cruelty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6042.context: A king orders a bad man to be handed to thieves, while night soldiers speak to a demon lord.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6043.meaning: It teaches that people seek mercy and that pleading can change harsh decisions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6043.context: A woman kneels, cries, and pleads with the demon lord not to give her sins to others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6044.meaning: The lesson is that leaders may choose harsh solutions, but they must consider the consequences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6044.context: The demon lord agrees to give the ungrateful man to thieves, telling them to accept him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6045.meaning: This shows how punishment can be broken down into parts, making it easier to share with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6045.context: Servants with spears and hammers cut the man's sin into pieces and hand them to thieves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6046.meaning: It reminds us that even in bad situations, we should not harm those who are already suffering.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6046.context: Even under thieves' control, the sinner is not attacked; the king is told not to eat the ungrateful.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6047.meaning: The verse warns that the worst people are not cleansed by nature and must face judgment.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6047.context: The traitor is described as cruel, ungrateful, and the lowest, not eaten by worms or insects.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6049.meaning: It shows that even in death, people honor others with beauty and respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6049.context: A demon prepares a funeral for a goat lord, decorating with gems, perfumes, and many clothes.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6050.meaning: The story teaches that rituals help honor the dead, even when they are destroyed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6050.context: The king sets fire to the goat lord, and the demon lord performs funeral rites with rituals.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6097.meaning: True happiness comes from the whole process, not just the final result or reward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6097.context: People often feel joy only at the very end of a long journey or task.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6098.meaning: When your mind is clear and free from jealousy, you find lasting value and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6098.context: Wise people who understand deep truth have moved beyond seeing the world in pairs.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6100.meaning: Blindly chasing fun can make you lose control and feel weak instead of strong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6100.context: Some people act happy like gods but are actually overwhelmed by their own pleasures.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6101.meaning: Working hard and being skilled brings happiness, while being lazy only brings you pain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6101.context: The text compares different states of being, linking laziness to pain and skill to joy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6102.meaning: Stay focused on the highest good, and you will not be shaken by bad luck or hate.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6102.context: A person who has reached the highest spiritual state remains calm through all life events.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6103.meaning: Wise people do not get stuck in daily ups and downs, but fools do.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6103.context: The world is full of many places that cause sadness and many that bring joy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6104.meaning: If you control your senses and stay humble, sadness and grief cannot hurt you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6104.context: The text praises those who are wise, kind, and have mastered their own desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6106.meaning: You should release anything that hurts you or holds you back from growing.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6106.context: This verse advises letting go of things that cause suffering or block your progress.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6107.meaning: Giving up selfish wants brings true joy, while chasing them leads to ruin and pain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6107.context: The text compares two paths, one of letting go and one of chasing wants.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6108.meaning: Worldly pleasures are tiny and fading, so they are not worth seeking over peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6108.context: This verse compares worldly fun to the highest spiritual bliss available to humans.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6109.meaning: Your past deeds determine your nature now, so act wisely to shape your future.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6109.context: The text explains how past actions shape who we are in this current life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6110.meaning: Life is full of ups and downs, so do not cling too tightly to any feeling.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6110.context: The passage describes how feelings of pain and pleasure constantly shift and change.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6111.meaning: When you pull your senses back from outside distractions, your inner self finds peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6111.context: A tortoise pulls its limbs in to stay safe, and the mind should do the same.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6113.meaning: When you think only of yourself, you create regret and fail to see the bigger picture.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6113.context: The text warns about the danger of thinking everything is about your own ego.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6114.meaning: When you stop fearing loss or craving gain, you reach a state of deep spiritual unity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6114.context: The verse describes a state of mind where fear and strong emotions have vanished.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6115.meaning: To find real peace, you must let go of both joy and sorrow and stay balanced.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6115.context: The text advises leaving behind both good and bad things to find true calm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6400.meaning: Truth speaks clearly to everyone. Listen to wisdom that guides your life with clarity and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6400.context: Saraswati appears as a divine voice heard by all listeners in the ancient story.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6401.meaning: Sometimes life feels empty and dark. Trust that this quiet time is just a pause.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6401.context: The sky is silent and still while sun and moon vanish from view.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6402.meaning: Change often starts in hidden places. Be ready for new forces that shape your world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6402.context: Darkness rises from the water and wind begins to stir the deep waves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6403.meaning: Silence can hide activity. Do not judge by appearances alone because truth is often hidden.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6403.context: A vessel seems silent until wind fills it with water and makes noise.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6404.meaning: Pressure can make you feel trapped. Keep moving forward even when things feel heavy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6404.context: The sky feels low when blocked by water while wind blows through the ocean.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6405.meaning: External power does not guarantee inner peace. True calm comes from within your own heart.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6405.context: Wind blows in the ocean but does not bring peace to those in heaven.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6406.meaning: Goodness shines even in chaos. Stay bright and hopeful when life feels dark and confusing.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6406.context: Rama shines brightly during the conflict between wind and water while the sky darkens.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6407.meaning: Love grounds us in trouble. When you care deeply, chaos settles and peace returns.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_6407.context: One who falls into the sky stands with affection while conflict becomes grounded.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7327.meaning: Think before you speak. Use your wisdom to choose kind words. This helps you avoid bad karma and stay on the right path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7327.context: The text explains that every action brings a result. You must use your mind to guide your words carefully.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7330.meaning: Keep your mind clear and focused on truth. Avoid lying or selfish wants. This brings peace and helps you connect with others gently.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7330.context: Focus your mind on all living beings with care. Do not let false thoughts or strong desires control your meditation practice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7331.meaning: Speak kindly and honestly. Avoid violence in your words. This practice purifies your mind and helps you live a righteous and peaceful life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7331.context: Yoga practice wakes up the mind through good speech. You must speak the truth without hurting anyone or using bad words.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7332.meaning: Control your mind with wisdom. Wild thoughts lead to bad actions. Use good deeds to calm your spirit and find inner balance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7332.context: The intellect guides the mind like a horse. If the mind is wild, actions become dark. Good actions balance this energy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7333.meaning: Be patient in all you do. Control your mind, speech, and body. This prevents suffering and helps you live a happy and peaceful life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7333.context: Bad actions lead to suffering and bad places. You must practice patience in your thoughts, words, and physical actions every day.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7335.meaning: Do not take what is not yours. Misunderstanding leads to confusion. Seek true knowledge to guide your life in the right direction.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7335.context: People who steal are like scattered sheep. They misunderstand the world and go the wrong way because they lack true understanding.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7336.meaning: Drop selfish and dark habits. They block your joy. Choose light and goodness to find real happiness and peace in your daily life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7336.context: Those who act with greed and darkness are cast aside. Leave these bad habits behind to find true happiness and spiritual freedom.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7337.meaning: Live simply and control your desires. Detach from material things. This freedom brings deep peace and helps you focus on what truly matters.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7337.context: A wise person is free from attachments. They live simply, eat lightly, and control their senses while living in quiet solitude.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7488.meaning: Even when we stop using senses, our thoughts can still be good if they are guided by virtue.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7488.context: After freeing senses, the speaker sees thoughts that do not follow, but share good qualities.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7489.meaning: When we are confused, our actions are short-lived and give only short joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7489.context: The mind is dark, so actions are fleeting and bring only temporary happiness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7490.meaning: When we cling to thoughts, darkness grows, and we cannot fully let go.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7490.context: Things linked with the mind do not fully disappear, and darkness rises like a shadow.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7491.meaning: Every act has a deeper value that others can see, and it feels correct when it is true.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7491.context: All actions have a higher quality that is counted by others, but some things feel right.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7492.meaning: Our inner feelings help us understand the world, and we become aware of that knowledge.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7492.context: The collective mind says that the feeling in the mind is the one who knows the field.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7493.meaning: Even a small action can speak forever because all living things are always here.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7493.context: How can a cut be eternal speech? Because all beings are naturally present.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7494.meaning: When we merge with the larger whole, we give up our ego and cannot keep our good nature.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7494.context: Like a river joining the ocean, we lose our name and do not control the loss of good qualities.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7495.meaning: Things can repeat in memory when we join with others and move away from the center.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7495.context: Where can a noun repeat in the past? When a living being mixes with others and leaves the middle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7513.meaning: True peace comes from controlling anger and being content. When you are selfless and calm, you find inner joy and stability.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7513.context: The text describes people who control their actions and desires. They are kind and happy with what they have.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7515.meaning: Do not trust loud words or public fame. Real virtue is quiet and sincere, not shown off for applause or attention.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7515.context: This verse warns against fake behavior in society. It says public praise and arguments are often empty and misleading.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7516.meaning: Stay balanced when people praise or criticize you. Keeping a steady mind and good character leads to a happy life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7516.context: A good person treats praise and blame the same way. They stay calm and kind regardless of what others say.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7517.meaning: Be kind to all living things. Keep your mind calm and deep, so outside chaos does not disturb your inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7517.context: The wise person helps everyone without hate. Like a deep lake, they remain calm even when others are upset.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7518.meaning: Live without fear and show respect to everyone. When you are brave and humble, you gain true wisdom and understanding.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7518.context: That we should not fear anyone. We should also treat all beings with respect and kindness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7528.meaning: Always aim to do good deeds. Focus on right actions and sacred thoughts to keep your life on a proper path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7528.context: A good person always wants to do what is right. They focus on duty and holy words in their daily life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7529.meaning: Avoid bad habits and choose good ones. Always be kind to visitors, as hospitality brings blessings and strengthens community bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7529.context: The wise person avoids harmful things and embraces good ones. They are always ready to welcome guests with open arms.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7530.meaning: Practice self-control in your eating habits. Discipline in daily routines helps you master your desires and stay focused.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7530.context: This verse speaks about discipline in daily routines. It suggests fasting and controlling hunger at specific times of day.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7505.meaning: Your actions directly shape your future. Choose good deeds to find peace and avoid fear in your daily life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7505.context: A seeker asks a wise sage about the causes of joy and sorrow in human life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7506.meaning: Leading by example requires discipline. When leaders control their impulses, they inspire trust and respect from their community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7506.context: Ancient texts praise self-control for everyone, but especially for priests who guide others in spiritual matters.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7507.meaning: Real success needs hard work. Combine learning with self-control to build a strong and honest character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7507.context: True purity comes from strict discipline, studying sacred texts, and practicing restraint in all aspects of life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7508.meaning: Mastering your own mind brings true power. When you are calm and controlled, you gain respect and inner strength.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7508.context: Self-restraint brings honor and holiness. A person who controls themselves becomes fearless and achieves great status.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7509.meaning: Inner calm brings lasting joy. When you control your mind, you feel happy and content every single day.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7509.context: A disciplined person finds peace in both sleep and waking hours, enjoying a balanced and happy life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7510.meaning: Patience stops you from hurting others. Watch your own behavior closely to fix mistakes before they grow.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7510.context: Restraint prevents anger from burning out of control. It helps you see your own flaws clearly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7511.meaning: Chaos hurts society. We need rules and leaders to keep order when people cannot control their own actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7511.context: Uncontrolled people are dangerous and feared. Kings were created to manage those who lack self-discipline.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7512.meaning: Discipline is the key to success. It unlocks the greatest blessings and helps you live a righteous life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7512.context: Self-control is the most vital virtue in every stage of life and brings the best rewards.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7548.meaning: Understand your thoughts, Sanjaya, and reflect on the situation. This will help you comprehend the world better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7548.context: In the Hindu epic Mahabharata, Sanjaya speaks to King Dhritarashtra, reminding him of his son Sanjaya's thoughts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7549.meaning: Without Sharia, you are vulnerable and controlled by others. Stick to religious guidelines for protection and self-respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7549.context: During the war at Kurukshetra, Parashurama addresses the king, emphasizing the importance of following Sharia (religious laws).

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7550.meaning: Wisdom comes from knowing the world, while detachment leads to peace and freedom from worldly desires.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7550.context: Uttamashloka, a sage, talks about wisdom and detachment.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7551.meaning: Ignore others' actions and focus on your own path. Hatred towards others won't solve anything.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7551.context: Parashurama addresses the king, emphasizing the importance of not being affected by the actions of others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7568.meaning: Knowledge is neutral and doesn't judge or compare. Acceptance and detachment lead to inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7568.context: Uttamashloka, a sage, talks about the nature of knowledge.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7569.meaning: Peace comes from within, not from external circumstances. Stay calm and centered, regardless of what happens around you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7569.context: Parashurama advises the king to focus on inner peace and not get affected by external events.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7570.meaning: Knowledge is neutral and doesn't judge or compare. Acceptance and detachment lead to inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7570.context: Uttamashloka, a sage, talks about the nature of knowledge.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7571.meaning: Detachment from material possessions and worldly desires brings inner peace and happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7571.context: Parashurama addresses the king, emphasizing the importance of detachment and inner peace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7532.meaning: Being honest and steady in your actions makes you a true person of high moral character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7532.context: A student of life joins his wife and stays true to his vows and duties.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7533.meaning: Giving food to others without harming animals is a pure gift that brings spiritual peace and joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7533.context: The text discusses how giving food without eating meat yourself creates a pure and holy act.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7534.meaning: When you share your food with others selflessly, you gain the sweet reward of true happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7534.context: A host treats his guests and servants with great care and shares his food with them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7535.meaning: Controlling your desire to eat shows strong self-discipline and helps you reach higher spiritual goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7535.context: A person controls his hunger and does not eat just because he feels like eating food.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7536.meaning: Eating only after sharing with others shows respect, while eating first is seen as selfish and wrong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7536.context: Food should be offered to gods and ancestors first, then to servants and guests before eating.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7537.meaning: Living a holy life brings divine protection and fills your home with joy and spiritual presence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7537.context: Those who follow these rules live in a blessed home surrounded by divine beings and peace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7538.meaning: Honoring your ancestors and gods through sharing food ensures your family line thrives and prospers.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7538.context: People who share meals with gods and ancestors enjoy blessings that last for many generations.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7539.meaning: Your choices determine your fate, so always choose good actions to create a better life for yourself.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7539.context: Every action a person takes in this world has consequences that shape their future destiny.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7628.meaning: Do not let time steal your good deeds. Hold on to your values before they fade.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7628.context: A wise speaker warns Indra that time destroys all things and gives them away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7629.meaning: Anger hurts others. Learn from mistakes and follow the eternal truth of kindness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7629.context: The speaker admits past anger caused pain and now understands the true path of life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7630.meaning: You cannot find full peace in others. True strength comes from within your own soul.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7630.context: The speaker reflects on how relying on others makes one feel incomplete and amazed.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7632.meaning: Everything in the world is connected. Understand that all life is under one great power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7632.context: The speaker claims control over all beings, from gods to demons, and asks Indra to know this.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7633.meaning: When you are lost, seek the light of wisdom. It will guide you to the right path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7633.context: Fishermen are confused and approach a direction where a divine figure named Vairocana is honored.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7634.meaning: Keep your mind calm and focused. Do not let regret or doubt control your thoughts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7634.context: The speaker tells Indra that their mind is steady and does not regret past actions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7635.meaning: Life brings both joy and pain. Accept your role and share the burdens with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7635.context: A hero is born into a family, and life is seen as a shared duty of suffering.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7636.meaning: Surround yourself with wise and good people. They will help you live a happy life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7636.context: Foolish people and Indra appear, and the text suggests life should be happy with good helpers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7741.meaning: When you lose loved ones or riches, remember that grief is natural, but focus on moving forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7741.context: A warrior is tied by Varuna's ropes and struck by Vajra, asking why mourn lost wife and wealth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7742.meaning: Hardship is part of life; do not dwell on regret, but learn to endure and grow.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7742.context: A body is destroyed, and the speaker says not to regret the hard times, questioning who would live in Tarailokya's ruin.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7743.meaning: Even strong criticism can be overcome by calm understanding and wise conversation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7743.context: Harsh words are defeated by darkness; Sukham, Bali, and Vairocana discuss the situation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7744.meaning: Powerful leaders must listen and learn, even when they feel strong and in control.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7744.context: Indra asks what was told when he was restrained, and Purandara sees him with a raised thunderbolt.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7745.meaning: Strength can grow from weakness, but harsh words should be used carefully and wisely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7745.context: Someone was once weak but became strong, asking who can speak cruel words.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7746.meaning: Showing kindness to those you control shows true power and earns respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7746.context: A person shows mercy to an enemy under his control, proving he is captured by a hero.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7747.meaning: Confusion in conflict leads to loss; clarity helps choose the right path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7747.context: Uncertainty causes two sides to fight, with one winning and one losing.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7748.meaning: Even the powerful can be humbled; respect everyone and stay humble.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_7748.context: A chief of gods warns not to become like this, saying God is conquered by all beings' might.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8186.meaning: Our thoughts can trick us into seeing things wrongly. We must learn to see past these mental illusions to find truth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8186.context: The text describes how the mind creates illusions that lead to destruction and confusion in the world.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8187.meaning: Work and daily tasks are part of life. We should do our duties with care and respect for others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8187.context: This verse lists daily human activities like farming and building homes that people perform to survive and live.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8188.meaning: Seek guidance from wise teachers. Their understanding helps us navigate life with clarity and purpose every day.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8188.context: Wise people follow those who truly understand others and speak with kindness and deep knowledge of life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8189.meaning: Knowledge is the key to spiritual freedom. Learning about life and others leads to the best destination.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8189.context: True freedom comes from deep knowledge of all beings. This wisdom is the highest goal for seekers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8191.meaning: Life takes many forms. Understanding these differences helps us respect all creatures and see the bigger picture.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8191.context: All living beings are born in four main ways. The wise observe these categories and the nature of life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8192.meaning: Learn to tell apart what is temporary and what is permanent. This clarity helps you make better choices.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8192.context: We must distinguish between things that change and things that stay the same in our daily observations.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8193.meaning: Different paths have different effects. Choose steps that heal and help you grow rather than those that harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8193.context: The text compares different types of feet or steps, noting that some are healing while others are many.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8194.meaning: Recognize the difference between spiritual healing and earthly needs. Feed your spirit with what truly nourishes it.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8194.context: Some beings are connected to healing while others are earthly. Horses eat food that is separate from the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8325.meaning: Align your daily deeds with spiritual truth to avoid inner conflict and confusion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8325.context: A seeker asks how to follow divine will without conflicting actions in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8326.meaning: Respect wisdom wherever it comes from and honor those who share true knowledge.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8326.context: A sage honors his son's wise reply by worshipping the sacred words spoken.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8327.meaning: Your social role does not limit your spiritual success if you live rightly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8327.context: All life stages can reach the highest goal if they follow the right path.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8328.meaning: Control your strong emotions to achieve peace and honor in your spiritual journey.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8328.context: One who masters desire and hatred through proper practice finds glory in the afterlife.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8329.meaning: Surrender to the divine to find a place of pure equality and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8329.context: Taking refuge in the supreme truth leads to a rankless state in heaven.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8330.meaning: Serve your guide with humility and focus to gain true knowledge and skill.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8330.context: A student lives with a teacher without jealousy to learn duty and wealth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8331.meaning: True learning requires deep devotion to your guide rather than just busy work.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8331.context: A hungry seeker must go beyond mere action to find refuge in the teacher.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8332.meaning: Serve others with humility and diligence to grow in wisdom and character daily.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8332.context: A humble disciple rises to serve the master and does all required tasks.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8651.meaning: We should honor the highest power that guides everything in our lives with sincere love and total trust.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8651.context: People praise the supreme divine power who rules over all worlds with great respect and deep devotion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8652.meaning: God is present in every part of creation, so we should see the divine in all living beings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8652.context: The speaker acknowledges that the Lord is the entire universe, including all moving and still things.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8653.meaning: True learning happens when we listen with focus and let wisdom settle deep within our hearts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8653.context: Tejas listens carefully to the gods words and absorbs the teaching into his own inner self.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8654.meaning: Divine presence supports both active duty and peaceful withdrawal, guiding us through every stage of life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8654.context: The Lord accepts worship and takes up fire, showing his presence in both action and renunciation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8655.meaning: When negative emotions pass, deeper spiritual truths can appear, revealing realities that go beyond our normal sight.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8655.context: Anger fades away as a powerful female spirit emerges from beyond the known boundaries of the universe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8656.meaning: Sacred figures may look fierce or strange, but their appearance symbolizes power and protection rather than harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_12_8656.context: The spirit appears dressed in black with red eyes, wearing divine jewelry and ornaments on her body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_811.context: The goddess identifies herself as the mother of the world and earth, married to the ascetic Shiva.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_812.meaning: God is generous and ready to give gifts to those who approach him with humility and sincere respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_812.context: The Lord mentions his son Sambo and offers eight boons to a devotee who bows her head in respect.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_964.meaning: God is seen everywhere in the world. His power and beauty are visible in all living things.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_964.context: The text describes the physical form of a divine being using rich colors and strong body parts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_965.meaning: The divine presence is huge and all-encompassing. It covers every part of the universe completely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_965.context: This verse lists many large body parts to show the immense size and power of the divine figure.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_966.meaning: Life gives us nourishment and strength. We should appreciate the hidden gifts that sustain our daily existence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_966.context: The passage uses strange names and body parts to describe the mysterious and hidden nature of reality.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_968.meaning: Every small detail in nature matters. The divine is found in the tiniest parts of the physical world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_968.context: The text mentions hair and nails to describe the detailed and complex nature of the divine body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_969.meaning: Wisdom and nature are connected to the divine. We find spiritual truth in the forces of the earth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_969.context: Sages and natural elements like wind and fire are linked to the divine form in this poetic description.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_970.meaning: Knowledge and truth guide our actions. Sacred wisdom helps us move through life with clarity and purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_970.context: Sacred texts and rituals are compared to body parts, showing they are essential parts of the divine whole.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_972.meaning: Generosity and stability bring peace. We should value the steady support that helps us grow and thrive.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_972.context: Gold, gifts, and stable places are mentioned to describe the wealth and security provided by the divine.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_973.meaning: Time and ritual help us stay connected to the divine. Regular practice keeps our spiritual life strong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_973.context: Sacrifices and time cycles are described as parts of a larger ritual that honors the divine order.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1037.meaning: God is known by many names. Using these names helps devotees connect with the divine presence and feel close to the Lord.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1037.context: The supreme deity is honored by his many names. The kind Lord establishes these names for his devoted followers to use.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1038.meaning: Leading others is hard. True believers must endure many life cycles and challenges before they achieve spiritual freedom and inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1038.context: Among all people, the leaders are special. Believers face many lifetimes and struggles before they find true peace and freedom.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1039.meaning: Worldly pleasure feels good but traps us. True happiness comes from looking beyond temporary joys and seeking deeper spiritual truth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1039.context: People stand on the path, awake or asleep. They find joy in worldly things but are trapped by their own satisfaction.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1040.meaning: Pure hearts attract divine love. When you are sincere and clean inside, devotion to God grows naturally and fills your life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1040.context: Devotion grows in those with pure hearts. This deep love for God arises naturally in beings who are truly sincere.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1041.meaning: Liberation is rare and difficult. Even powerful beings struggle to reach it, so humans must work hard with faith and effort.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1041.context: The source of total freedom is everywhere. This state is very hard to reach for gods and even harder for humans.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1042.meaning: Steady faith brings peace. Through divine grace, unwavering devotion helps people calm their minds and reach the highest spiritual state.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1042.context: Devotion to Rudra is steady and strong. By his grace, people gain this devotion and find perfect peace in their minds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1043.meaning: Surrender leads to freedom. When you give up your ego and trust God, he helps you escape the endless cycle of birth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1043.context: Those who have realized all beings are one. The compassionate God helps those who surrender to him escape the cycle of life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1044.meaning: Focus on the supreme. Only by dedicating your efforts and penance to the highest God can you truly escape worldly bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1044.context: Other gods do not grant final freedom. Only through the power of penance directed to Mahadeva can humans achieve liberation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1175.meaning: Even when happy, we must plan for future needs and not ignore practical concerns.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1175.context: A wise man looks around, feels joy, then worries about where he will live.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1176.meaning: Seek permission and respect others’ space before entering their life or home.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1176.context: He walks to the door, stands, and asks those beyond to let him stay.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1177.meaning: Beauty and grace can inspire awe, reminding us to appreciate the gifts around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1177.context: Seven beautiful maidens leave the house, surrounded by the lord’s presence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1178.meaning: Unwanted attraction can disturb peace; we should guard our thoughts and emotions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1178.context: A girl in the evening catches his eye, and he feels a heavy sadness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1179.meaning: Patience and guidance help us choose the right path and avoid harmful choices.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1179.context: A patient Brahmin appears, and wise people advise him to let the Lord enter elsewhere.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1188.meaning: Kindness and acceptance create strong bonds and mutual respect between people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1188.context: The Lord greets her warmly, and she embraces the sage with open arms.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1189.meaning: True steadiness in character helps us face difficult conversations with calmness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1189.context: The sage remains unchanged, like a wooden hut, while she talks to him sadly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1190.meaning: We should focus on devotion rather than fleeting desires to find lasting peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1190.context: A Brahman speaks about lustful patience, urging worship and devotion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1166.meaning: When you face challenges with a good heart, you will find balance and fair rewards in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1166.context: A hero travels across the land, moving north over a mountain range with a clear purpose.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1168.meaning: Nature provides constant beauty and nourishment, reminding us to appreciate the simple gifts of the earth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1168.context: The traveler finds a lush forest filled with trees, fruit, and birds that stay all year round.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1169.meaning: True peace is found in sacred spaces where the beauty of the world supports your inner calm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1169.context: A sage finds a holy place where mountains shine with gold and gems near a calm lake.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1170.meaning: When you look within yourself, the beauty of the world brings you a deep and lasting happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1170.context: The wise man sees many lovely spots and feels deep joy while meditating on his own soul.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1171.meaning: Inner strength and wisdom can create a life that is more valuable than any material treasure.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1171.context: He builds a golden home covered in gems that looks even better than the king of wealth's palace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1172.meaning: The universe is full of wonder and variety, showing that there is always something new to admire.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1172.context: The scene shows palaces that look like mountains, flying chariots, and many different kinds of shiny gems.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1173.meaning: Even small paths in life can be filled with beauty and power if you look closely at them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1173.context: A narrow river flows with flowers and is decorated with shining gems and thunderbolts on the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1174.meaning: Surrounding yourself with good and beautiful things helps your mind feel calm, safe, and happy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1174.context: Buildings have gem arches and pearl nets, creating a view that is full of auspicious and lovely things.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1244.meaning: Respect those who guide you because they care about your well being and future success.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1244.context: A wise man explains he was sent by the bride father to give advice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1245.meaning: Trust that doing the right thing leads to safety and honor in your life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1245.context: The speaker promises safe return and no shame for the brahmin who will gain a daughter.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1246.meaning: True wisdom is rare and powerful, so value deep answers that challenge your understanding of reality.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1246.context: Kamy asked a question and received an answer that is hard for all worlds to surpass.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1247.meaning: Patience and obedience to wise guidance help you achieve good results in your spiritual journey.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1247.context: The speaker tells the sage Ashtavakra to go do well and wait for further instructions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1248.meaning: Honor wise teachers by listening to them and respecting their role in your spiritual growth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1248.context: The speaker says he served a sage and spoke to honor him before the heavenly beings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1257.meaning: Seek to understand the deep connection between the divine source and its physical symbols.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1257.context: The question asks what brahmins say about the eternal vessel Brahman and the Lingam symbol.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1258.meaning: Living a simple disciplined life dedicated to spiritual truth earns respect and inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1258.context: It describes those who follow the path of the Lingam as ascetics who are respected.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1259.meaning: Good deeds like charity and prayer are valuable when done with a pure heart.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1259.context: The question asks about the value of sacrifice poetry and charity for purified people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1786.meaning: Anger toward wise teachers leads to personal failure and loss of respect from others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1786.context: Respect for wise teachers brings success to society and individuals who follow their guidance.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1788.meaning: Doing wrong things leads to defeat and loss, just like losing something in the ocean.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1788.context: Bad actions are like a fruit thrown into the deep sea and lost forever.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1789.meaning: Nature and divine signs remind us of the beauty and order present in the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1789.context: The moon and sea show natural beauty, while divine marks show spiritual power and grace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1790.meaning: Faith and rituals connect us to divine power, bringing strength and spiritual growth to life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1790.context: Divine power works through rituals and sacrifices, showing the strength of faith and devotion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1791.meaning: A pure person finds peace by respecting wise teachers and controlling their own desires.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1791.context: Seeking fame and fortune is common, but true peace comes from self-control and respect.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1792.meaning: Even divine beings show humility, teaching us to respect the earth and wise teachings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1792.context: The Lord shows deep humility by bowing to the earth after hearing wise words.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1793.meaning: Regular devotion and worship help you reach the best spiritual goals and inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1793.context: This story begins to teach that constant worship leads to the highest spiritual rewards.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1794.meaning: Wise teachers are rare and precious, serving as guides for all people in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1794.context: A wise teacher is born to help all beings and is respected by everyone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1912.meaning: Great beauty often brings great attention and danger. We must stay humble and aware of the risks that come with being admired.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1912.context: A wise sage named Deva Sharma lived with his wife Ruchira who was the most beautiful woman on earth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1913.meaning: Physical beauty can captivate even divine beings. It shows how powerful attraction is and how it can distract from duty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1913.context: Gods and demons were all charmed by her beauty. Indra the king of gods ruled over the celestial realm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1914.meaning: True care means taking active steps to protect those you love. Vigilance and effort are key to keeping family safe.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1914.context: The sage understood women well. He used all his strength and energy to keep his wife safe from harm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1915.meaning: Knowing the weaknesses of others helps us prepare. We must guard our loved ones against those who might exploit them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1915.context: He knew Indra was lustful. So he worked very hard to shield his wife from the gods unwanted advances.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1916.meaning: When we have important duties, we must plan ahead. Protecting our family remains a priority even during spiritual tasks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1916.context: The sage wanted to perform a holy ritual. He worried about how to keep his wife safe while he was away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1917.meaning: Seeking wisdom from trusted mentors is wise. We should not face difficult problems alone but ask for guidance from experts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1917.context: He thought deeply about safety. He called his disciple Vipula and spoke to the sage Bhrigu for advice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1918.meaning: Trust your family to help each other. Clear instructions and shared responsibility ensure that everyone stays safe and cared for.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1918.context: He told Indra he would leave for a ritual. He asked his son to protect his wife who prayed for others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1919.meaning: Evil or temptation often hides in disguise. We must stay awake and careful because danger does not always look obvious.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_1919.context: He warned that Indra changes forms. He told his son to stay alert because the god is tricky.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2064.meaning: Be patient and stay pure while waiting for the right partner to come into your life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2064.context: A young woman waits patiently for the right time to find a good husband.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2065.meaning: When you lose your true guide, you may find different words that do not help you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2065.context: A wise speaker explains how people lose their true partners or spiritual guides.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2066.meaning: Follow the right path even if you are not born into a specific family or clan.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2066.context: Manu gives rules about what is right for people who are not from your family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2067.meaning: Do not use force or show off money to get things, as this is not honest.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2067.context: People are described as using force or showing off wealth to get what they want.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2068.meaning: Be the guiding light for those who are searching for the truth in their lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2068.context: A blessing is given to someone who holds the hand of a truthful person.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2069.meaning: It is a great sin to lie to someone who is sincerely looking for wisdom.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2069.context: The text warns against lying to someone who is seeking deep spiritual knowledge.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2070.meaning: Everyone, from teachers to spouses, must tell the truth to avoid facing serious punishment.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2070.context: The text lists different people who face punishment for telling lies in their roles.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2071.meaning: Do not force others to speak or act against their will, as this brings shame.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2071.context: Manu criticizes forcing someone to speak or acting in a way that is not right.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2468.meaning: It shows that nature can be a constant source of beauty and peace for everyone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2468.context: Describes a garden with lotus trees and flowers that bloom all seasons, like a beautiful paradise.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2469.meaning: It reminds us that a good environment and cozy home help people feel safe and relaxed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2469.context: Talks about India’s cool climate and warm waters, and how its homes and beds are very comfortable.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2470.meaning: It teaches that generosity and abundance can make people feel welcomed and cared for.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2470.context: Mentions golden couches and mattresses, and endless food and drink spread everywhere for guests.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2471.meaning: It shows that all creatures, big or small, have a role and add life to the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2471.context: Lists various birds and insects, like parrots, bees, cuckoos, and centipedes, in a lively scene.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2472.meaning: It reminds us that every living thing is connected and part of a shared natural family.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2472.context: Names peacocks, chickens, and other animals as children of living beings in a forest setting.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2473.meaning: It illustrates how art and music can lift spirits and bring joy to those who witness them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2473.context: Describes beautiful apsaras and gandharvas dancing around a king in a grand hall.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2475.meaning: It teaches that music and knowledge together create harmony and inspire people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2475.context: Notes the sweet sound of songs and learning, and the king hearing swans singing nearby.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2476.meaning: It encourages us to question our experiences and seek truth in what we see.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2476.context: Shows the king reflecting on a wonderful sight, wondering if it is a dream or reality.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2961.meaning: Understanding that basic needs sustain life helps us value simple resources and care for others with compassion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2961.context: Sages explain that food sustains life and water is essential for all living beings on earth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2962.meaning: Helping others with basic needs like water brings deep joy and spiritual peace to your own soul.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2962.context: Giving water is praised as the best act because it supports life and brings peace to the giver.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2963.meaning: Kind acts like giving water protect you and bring lasting honor and safety in your life journey.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2963.context: The text praises the fame and longevity gained by giving water, comparing it to a protective cloud.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2964.meaning: Selfless giving leads to lasting happiness and spiritual freedom, freeing you from guilt and negative karma.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2964.context: Those who give water achieve their desires and eternal fame, reaching a state beyond sin after death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2965.meaning: True charity includes meeting basic human needs like food and clothing, not just ritual offerings alone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2965.context: The speaker asks about gifts of sesame and lamps, then requests basic food and clothes for themselves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2967.meaning: Ancient stories teach us timeless lessons about duty and justice through the dialogue of wise figures.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2967.context: The narrator introduces an ancient story about a conversation between a Brahmin priest and the god Yama.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2968.meaning: Living in harmony with nature and community creates a stable environment for spiritual growth and learning.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2968.context: A large village of priests lived in the central region between two major rivers and a mountain.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2969.meaning: Facing difficult or scary situations is part of life, reminding us to stay calm and accept reality.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_2969.context: Yama, the god of death, appears to a man with dark clothes, red eyes, and a fierce look.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3020.meaning: This scene sets the stage for a story about how we seek help and find relief.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3020.context: A woman arrives at a grassy well where people are waiting for water to drink.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3022.meaning: We often feel embarrassed when we need help, but accepting it can bring us peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3022.context: Thirsty people ask for water at the well and feel deep shame about their situation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3023.meaning: Sometimes we face huge problems that seem impossible to solve with our own strength.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3023.context: A giant lizard appears near the well, and many people try to lift it up.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3024.meaning: When our efforts fail, we should turn to a higher power for guidance and help.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3024.context: They tie the giant creature with strong straps but cannot move it, so they seek Krishna.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3025.meaning: We must accept that we cannot fix everything alone and need divine intervention.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3025.context: The giant lizard stands still, and the people realize they have no one else to save them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3026.meaning: Good actions do not always prevent bad situations, so we must trust the greater plan.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3026.context: A character asks another why they are in such a bad place despite doing good deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3028.meaning: We should remember past blessings and ask how our actions affect our current life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3028.context: Someone recalls receiving many cows from a king in the past and asks what happened.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3029.meaning: Generosity and kindness can lead to unexpected rewards and positive changes in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3029.context: A woman counts a thousand cows given to her by a Brahmin who wanted to change.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3040.meaning: Good actions are noticed by higher powers and should be honored with gratitude.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3040.context: Yama praised the king for his many good deeds and thanked him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3041.meaning: Ignorance can lead to sin, so learning and awareness are important.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3041.context: Yama warned that the king made a mistake because he did not know better.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3042.meaning: False promises and deceit harm others and must be avoided.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3042.context: Yama questioned a Brahmin who claimed protection but was actually lying.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3043.meaning: Admitting mistakes is hard, but honesty is necessary for growth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3043.context: The Lord said he would first struggle, then fall, and not tell the king about his wrongs.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3044.meaning: Faith in a higher power can bring relief from difficult situations.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3044.context: Yama spoke loudly to Vasudeva, saying Krishna would help him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3045.meaning: Even after many wrongs, one can find lasting peace through right actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3045.context: After a thousand years of bad deeds, the king will reach eternal peace by conquering worlds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3046.meaning: Failure to achieve goals can leave one feeling lost and uncertain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3046.context: The speaker saw someone fall into a well and felt he had not reached the promised place.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3047.meaning: Penance and devotion can lead to spiritual liberation and reward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_3047.context: The speaker thanked Krishna for saving him and asked to go to heaven.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4461.meaning: True goodness is shown by doing right things and living with deep respect for sacred values.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4461.context: The text describes the key traits that define a truly holy and righteous person in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4462.meaning: Good deeds matter most when done alone, proving your character is strong and genuine.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4462.context: People honor those who act with integrity, even if no one is watching their actions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4463.meaning: Ignoring wisdom and choosing wickedness kills your spirit, making you spiritually empty and lost.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4463.context: The passage warns against people who ignore spiritual guides and choose to do evil things.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4464.meaning: Lacking self-control and moral limits shortens your life and leads to suffering in the afterlife.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4464.context: This verse warns that loose boundaries and bad sexual habits lead to a short, bad life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4465.meaning: Some people survive a long time without virtue, but this does not make their life truly good.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4465.context: It mentions that some people live long lives despite having very few good qualities.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4466.meaning: Being calm, honest, and gentle toward others helps you live a long and peaceful life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4466.context: The text lists calmness, truthfulness, and kindness as traits that help people live long.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4467.meaning: Even the poorest and most ignored people can find deep worth and dignity in their lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4467.context: This describes a person who is lost, poor, and eats scraps, yet finds great value.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4468.meaning: Start your day with calm thoughts on duty and goals, then wash up and stand with respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4468.context: The verse advises waking up early to meditate on duty and wealth before starting the day.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4602.meaning: The best teacher is one who stays humble and keeps learning like a student always.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4602.context: A teacher tells a student to act with the wisdom and maturity of an elder.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4603.meaning: A wise guide helps you see the future clearly, so you can make better choices.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4603.context: A student tells his master that he cannot survive without the teacher's deep wisdom.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4604.meaning: It is better to stay quiet than to speak words that might hurt others or cause trouble.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4604.context: People of all skill levels speak, but wise people avoid saying things that cause harm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4605.meaning: We should try to understand why people act badly when they are hurting or in pain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4605.context: Arjuna asks his teacher to help him understand actions done with a broken heart.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4606.meaning: One bad leader can destroy a group, so we must be careful who we follow.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4606.context: The text warns that a bad elder can ruin the whole family and destroy its future.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4608.meaning: Small things can hold big memories, and we should remember the people who helped us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4608.context: A mixed verse mentions a fig tree flower and a person named Mogha in a story.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4609.meaning: Bad actions by one person can hurt the reputation of the whole family or group.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_4609.context: The text says that having a bad person in your family brings shame to everyone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5386.meaning: God can change his appearance instantly to teach us that true power is hidden behind simple looks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5386.context: A divine figure appears suddenly in a fierce form to show power and command attention from the onlookers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5387.meaning: We should help others because every person shares the same human experience and needs support today.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5387.context: A woman surrounded by spirits asks for help, showing that everyone faces similar struggles in life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5388.meaning: Pure intentions flow like holy rivers, bringing blessings and peace to every place they touch.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5388.context: She holds a sacred pot filled with holy water, symbolizing purity and the flow of divine grace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5389.meaning: Small acts of love and respect please God more than grand gestures or expensive offerings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5389.context: She offers flowers and scents to the divine, showing deep respect and devotion through simple gifts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5390.meaning: When we pray with a humble heart, divine love surrounds us completely and protects us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5390.context: The lady joins her hands in prayer, and the goddess responds by covering everything in presence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5391.meaning: Life can become dark and still when we lose focus, so stay aware and keep faith.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5391.context: Darkness falls as eyes close, and the ritual stops, showing how quickly things can change.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5392.meaning: Fear spreads quickly in groups, but remember that darkness is only temporary and will pass soon.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5392.context: People feel great fear as the leader of spirits appears, making the world seem dark and cold.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5393.meaning: Wisdom shines like a bright light to guide us out of confusion and fear in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5393.context: A bright flame shoots from the forehead, bringing light back to the dark and confused world.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5567.meaning: Living honestly and peacefully brings joy and harmony even after life ends.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5567.context: People practiced fasting, vows, honesty, and peace, then joined heavenly singers after death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5568.meaning: Preparing a calm space and sharing with nature helps a righteous person find inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5568.context: A yogi set up a frog-shaped bed and enjoyed company of serpents.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5569.meaning: Respecting nature’s gifts and learning new skills can lead to spiritual growth and travel.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5569.context: A man ate grass released by a deer and traveled to Amaravati after initiation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5570.meaning: Helping the humble and practicing cool, calm yoga brings one closer to supreme truth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5570.context: Serving algae or rotting leaves is praised; carrying cold yoga leads to ultimate goal.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5571.meaning: Simplicity in diet and trust in resources can bring joy and divine companionship.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5571.context: Eating air, water, fruits, or roots, he trusted wealth and enjoyed apsara hosts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5572.meaning: Consistent ritual practice over time can transform a person into a wise leader.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5572.context: Agniyogavaha performed summer rituals; after twelve years, a king emerged.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5573.meaning: Strict discipline and respectful handling of death can elevate a person to leadership.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5573.context: A sage followed dietary rules for twelve years; a king emerged by processing the dead.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5574.meaning: Embracing purity and celebrating new beginnings at a young age fosters spiritual confidence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5574.context: Sathandile surrounded pure sky, entered a house, and celebrated initiation at twelve.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5705.meaning: Having resources for others shows care, and sharing meets both personal wants and community needs.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5705.context: People had many wells and ponds to help others, and they also had everyday needs and desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5706.meaning: Material wealth can support life, but true value comes from using it to grow and help others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5706.context: A man owned a seat, bed, carriage, wealth, gems, houses, cows, and women, producing crops.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5707.meaning: Kindness and good thoughts lead to a better rebirth, showing actions shape future life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5707.context: A generous man with a good mind is reborn in a heavenly world after death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5708.meaning: Human life is a chance to collect resources and learn responsibility for future growth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5708.context: Heavenly beings are born as humans to gather wealth and grain in the family of Mahabhoga.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5710.meaning: Desire and happiness can drive success, but true richness comes from balanced, purposeful living.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5710.context: He was filled with desire and joy, and his enjoyment and treasures made him rich.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5711.meaning: Wisdom and generosity bring spiritual insight, connecting people to higher truths.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5711.context: Old men and the charitable enjoyed these blessings, seeing visions of the Supreme Personality mentioned by Brahma.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5712.meaning: Mercy is important, but giving without asking shows humility and respect for divine gifts.
